articles.title: Reading a 150 MB playlist on a 4 GB TV box without running out of memory
articles.excerpt: I build NewTV Player, a media player for people's own playlists (an M3U link or an Xtream login from their provider). It runs on phones, Android TV boxes, Fire TV and Windows, and it is written in Rea…
articles.body: I build NewTV Player, a media player for people's own playlists (an M3U link or an Xtream login from their provider). It runs on phones, Android TV boxes, Fire TV and Windows, and it is written in React Native with Expo and SQLite. The hardest bug I have fixed in it had nothing to do with video. It was a JSON file. The bug: an empty playlist on a 4 GB box A user on an Android TV box with 4 GB of memory added their subscription. The progress bar moved, the app worked for a while, and then the playlist was simply empty. No crash report, no error on screen. The reason was size. Xtream panels answer three calls for a catalogue: live channels, films and series. Each one is a single JSON array. For real subscriptions we measured 72 MB in one list and 156 MB across the three .

articles.body: An order update can omit a packing note because that field has not changed. If an adapter turns every missing note into an empty value, a later status update can erase the instruction the warehouse still needs. Treat field presence as part of the data contract. For the small example below, an omitted packingNote leaves the current value alone, a nonblank string replaces it, and null explicitly clears it. This is an example contract to agree with both systems, not a claim about a particular store API. Decode intent before applying a value The JavaScript ?? operator is not enough for this contract: a fallback for null and undefined would collapse the explicit clear into the same path as an absent value.

articles.body: Most AI coding sessions fail the same way: you describe a change, the model starts writing, and the decisions about what to build and how it fits together stay implicit. By the third prompt the context has drifted. bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD is an agile method for AI driven development that keeps those decisions explicit. articles.title: Turn one Claude Code session into a game studio with 49 agents
articles.excerpt: A solo game project in a single Claude Code chat tends to drift. Nothing stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping the design doc, or shipping spaghetti, because no one plays QA or asks whethe…
articles.body: A solo game project in a single Claude Code chat tends to drift. Nothing stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping the design doc, or shipping spaghetti, because no one plays QA or asks whether a feature fits the game's vision. Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios gives one Claude Code session the structure of a studio. The README lists 49 agents, 74 skills (slash commands), 15 hooks, 14 path-scoped rules and 62 document templates. You still make every decision, but a team of specialist agents asks questions and flags mistakes along the way. How the studio is organized Agents sit in three tiers, like a real studio: Directors: creative-director, technical-director, producer.

ElevenLabs offers a battle‑tested, cloud‑based voice cloning platform that is: Fast – training a model from a few minutes of audio takes less than a minute. articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

"Yes, you can even vote from space! All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .
